skills.name: Explorers, missions, traders and imperial agents in Africa

note.text: Explorers produced travel records and maps using assistance and knowledge from African guides and communities. Missionaries promoted religion and often education or translation. Traders sought commercial returns; statesmen and officials negotiated or imposed imperial claims; soldiers enforced expansion. Their activities could overlap but should not be treated as one occupation. Knowledge collected by travellers could assist later imperial projects, while African responses differed. A claimed contribution should be examined alongside coercion, extraction and the interests of those affected.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Explorers produced travel records and maps using assistance and knowledge from African guides and communities. Missionaries promoted religion and often education or translation. Traders sought commercial returns; statesmen and officials negotiated or imposed imperial claims; soldiers enforced expansion. Their activities could overlap but should not be treated as one occupation. Knowledge collected by travellers could assist later imperial projects, while African responses differed. A claimed contribution should be examined alongside coercion, extraction and the interests of those affected.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A travel map, a mission school record, a trading agreement and an official proclamation answer different historical questions. Stanley's activities in the Congo region can be related to Leopold's imperial project without confusing that region with Cameroon. African guides' contribution must not disappear simply because a European traveller authored the surviving book.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify actor, action, place and purpose. Distinguish an actor's stated motive from an effect of the activity. Do not assume every school or map had identical consequences. A source may advertise an imperial achievement while omitting the local costs or knowledge on which it depended.
